chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
«The woman seeking khul' is the one who says to her husband: 'Release me [from the marriage], and I will give you what I took from you.'»

And he said: «It is not permissible for him to take anything from her until she says: 'By Allah, I will not fulfill your oath, and I will not obey your command, and I will surely announce in your house without your permission, and I will make another man lie on your bed.'»

So if she does that without him knowing, what he took from her becomes permissible for him, and she is divorced with a divorce that is not followed by another, and she becomes irrevocably separated by that, and he is one of the suitors [who can remarry her without a new contract].»

key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَةُ: The woman seeking khul' (divorce by compensation)
key_terms.خَاطِبًا: Suitable for remarriage without a new contract

ai.seo_question: What are the specific conditions for a valid khul' divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the mechanism of *khul'* where the wife secures her release by offering compensation, specifically highlighting the condition that the husband may retain the gift only if she swears an irrevocable oath of separation in his absence. This specific form of *takhli'ah* renders the divorce *ba'in* (irrevocable), preventing the husband from easily reclaiming the wife without a new contract, a nuance emphasized by Shia jurists to protect the wife's agency in initiating the split. The ruling underscores the legal weight of unilateral oaths in marital dissolution within the Twelver Shi'a tradition.
